items.title: '메모리 후공정 장비사' 아테코, 코스닥 기술상장 도전
items.snippet: 메모리 반도체 후공정 장비 업체 아테코가 코스닥 상장예비심사 신청서를 지난 28일 한국거래소에 제출했다고 밝혔다.아테코는 기술특례상장으로 코스닥에 도전한다. 상장 주관사는 미래에셋증권과 IBK투자증권이다. 회사는 상장으로 확보한 자금으로 제품군을 강화할 계획이다. 기술특례상장은 기술력을 인정받은 기업이 수익성 등 일부 재무 요건을 충족하지 못하더라도 상장할 수 있도록 허용하는 제도다.회사는 메모리 자동화 검사 장비인 테스트 핸들러를 생산한다. 고대역폭메모리(HBM), LPCAMM(Low Power Compression Attache

items.title: 인텔-SAP, 피지컬 AI 협력...기업 전산-로봇 연결한다

items.title: 이비덴, 1조3000억원 투입해 CPU 기판 생산능력 확충
items.snippet: 일본 반도체 패키지 기판 업체 이비덴이 1조2800억원을 투입해 인공지능(AI) 서버용 고성능 반도체 패키지 기판 생산능력을 확대한다. 늘어나는 중앙처리장치(CPU) 패키지 기판 수요에 대응한다.이비덴은 29일 이사회를 열고 일본 기후현 가마 공장 6동의 CPU용 고성능 집적회로(IC) 패키지 기판 생산능력을 늘리기로 했다. 해외 생산거점도 투자할 계획이다. 신규 설비는 2029회계연도부터 순차 가동한다. 구체적인 생산능력 증가 규모는 공개하지 않았다.이비덴은 최근 AI 추론 연산 수요가 늘고 에이전틱 AI가 확산으로 CPU 기판

items.title: 깊어지는 체코 원전 갈등…대우건설, "한수원, 조단위 추가공사비 40%만 반영"

items.title: 해성디에스, 3분기 매출 2453억원…4년 만에 최대 경신
items.snippet: 해성디에스가 올해 3분기 역대 최대 분기 매출을 기록했다. 종전 최대였던 2022년 3분기(2243억원)를 4년 만에 넘어섰다. 해성디에스는 3분기 연결 기준 매출 2453억원, 영업이익 338억원을 기록했다고 29일 잠정 공시했다. 전년 대비 매출은 37.4%, 영업이익은 109.8% 증가했다. 전분기 대비로는 각각 16.2%, 35.9% 늘었다. 영업이익률은 13.8%로 전년보다 4.8%p, 전분기보다 2%p 상승했다. 3분기 누적 매출은 6451억원, 영업이익은 696억원이다. 전년 대비 각각 36.3%, 182% 증가했다.

items.snippet: 현대차[005380]가 현대차그룹 내 소프트웨어 중심 자동차(SDV) 개발 자회사 포티투닷에 2천852억원 규모의 출자를 단행한다고 29일 공시했다.현대차는 주주배정 유상증자에 참여해 포티투닷 보통주 221만주를 취득하는 출자를 진행할 예정이다.출자금은 오는 11월과 내년 4월에 분할해 납입된다.ebyun@yna.co.kr

items.snippet: 여론조사 업체 엠브레인퍼블릭·케이스탯리서치·코리아리서치·한국리서치의 정례 조사에서 범여권에서 거론되는 조희대 대법원장 탄핵 소추에 반대한다는 응답자가 45%, 찬성한다는 응답자가 34%인 것으로 나타났다. 이재명 대통령 국정 수행을 긍정적으로 평가한 응답자는 46%로 두 달 만에 부정 평가자 44%보다 많아졌다. 민주당 지지율도 3%포인트(p) 올랐다. 그러나 민주당에 대한 호감도는 6개월 전보다 크게 낮아진 것으로 나타났다.

items.snippet: 서울 ‘위례선’ 트램(노면전차) 개통이 또 연기됐다. 공정률 97%로 지난 2월 시운전까지 했지만 서울시와 경찰이 안전 심의 절차를 놓고 갈등을 빚었기 때문이다. 서울시는 28일 “올 12월 개통이 어려워졌다”며 “내년 상반기에 다시 개통 일정을 발표하겠다”고 밝혔다. 위례선은 지하철 5호선 마천역과 8호선 복정·남위례역을 잇는 5.4㎞ 노선이다. 위례신도시를 남북으로 관통한다. 사업비는 3503억원이다. 서울에서 트램이 달리는 건 1968년 운행이 중단된 이후 처음이다.

items.snippet: ‘호랑이와 곶감’이라는 전래동화가 있습니다. 울고 보채던 아이는 호랑이가 온다는 말에도 울음을 그치지 않지만, 곶감을 준다는 말에 울음을 그칩니다. 그럴 만큼 곶감이 맛있다는 이야기입니다. 달콤한 간식이 흔하지 않던 옛날, 감은 아이들은 물론 어른들도 좋아하는 과일이었습니다. 나무에서 따서 잘 익힌 홍시도, 햇볕과 바람에 말린 곶감도 사람들의 사랑을 받았습니다. 그런데 감은 단지 맛있는 먹거리였던 것만은 아니었습니다. 때로는 나라 사이의 외교 문제가 됐고, 임금의 죽음을 둘러싼 의혹의 중심에 서기도 했습니다.

items.title: [Dr.이은봉의 의학 연구 다이제스트] 만성 신질환자의 단백질 섭취 관행 뒤집혔다… 과도한 제한은 염증 악화로 신장 손상 빨라져
items.snippet: 신장은 수분량을 조절하고 대사과정에서 발생하는 각종 독소를 소변으로 배출한다. 만성 신질환은 당뇨병, 고혈압 등 다양한 원인에 의해서 이런 신장 기능이 떨어진 상태다. 더 진행되면 투석이 필요한 신부전 상태에 이른다. 그 과정에서 단백질을 과다 섭취하면, 대사과정에서 체내 독소가 만들어지고 신장 기능이 떨어질 수 있기 때문에 만성 신질환 환자에게 단백질 섭취를 제한하도록 권고했다.

items.title: 나이 들어 체중 변화 심하면 사망률 최대 62%↑
items.snippet: 나이 들어 체중 변화가 심한 사람일수록 사망률이 최대 62% 높다는 연구 결과가 나왔다. 서울대병원 강남센터 소화기내과 서지연·최지민 교수와 숭실대 한경도 교수 연구팀은 국민건강보험공단 자료를 활용해 2012년부터 2015년까지 건강검진을 받은 75세 이상 고령자 중 체중 측정 기록이 4회 이상 있는 총 61만 6696명을 분석했다. 평균 연령은 78세였다.

items.title: ‘후각’을 지켜야 인생의 후반이 감미롭다
items.snippet: 나이가 들면 눈이 침침해지고 귀가 어두워지는 것은 걱정하면서도 냄새를 맡는 능력이 떨어지는 데는 별 관심을 두지 않는다. 시력이 나빠지면 안경을 쓰고, 청력이 떨어지면 보청기를 찾지만, 후각이 약해지면 그저 나이 탓으로 돌리는 경우가 많다. 하지만 후각은 음식의 맛을 즐기는 감각일 뿐 아니라 영양 상태와 신체 기능, 뇌 건강에까지 영향을 미치는 중요한 감각이다. 후각은 오감 가운데 뇌와 가장 직접적으로 연결되는 감각 중 하나다. 코로 들어온 냄새 분자는 비강 천장 부근의 후각상피에 도달한다. 이곳에 있는 후각수용 신경세포가 냄새를 감지하면 신호가 뇌의 여러 영역으로 전달된다. 기억과 관련된 해마, 감정과 관련된 편도체 등과도 밀접하게 연결돼 있다. 어린 시절 어머니가 끓여주던 된장찌개 냄새를 맡으면 수십 년 전 기억이 떠오르고, 특정 향수를...

items.title: 뇌졸중 증상 암기법 ‘이웃·손·발·시선’
items.snippet: 매년 10월 29일은 세계뇌졸중기구(WSO)가 지정한 ‘세계 뇌졸중의 날’이다. 대한뇌졸중학회는 이날을 맞아 뇌졸중 경고 증상을 미리 알아두고, 의심 증상이 나타나면 지체 없이 119에 신고해 치료받을 것을 강조하고 있다. 지난 21~23일에는 세계뇌졸중학회가 서울 코엑스에서 열렸다. 뇌졸중 연구자와 임상의, 보건의료 전문가 2500여 명이 모여 뇌졸중 예방과 초급성기 치료 방안 등에 대해 논의했다. 뇌졸중은 뇌혈관이 막히는 뇌경색과 혈관이 터지는 뇌출혈로 나뉜다. 질병관리청 통계에 따르면, 2022년 뇌졸중 발생은 약 11만건이었으며, 발생 환자의 20%가 1년 이내 사망했다.

items.title: SLICE-CiM: Selective Layer-wise Inference Control Engine with Confidence-Based Early Exit for SRAM based Digital Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Digital SRAM compute-in-memory (CIM) macros enable energy-efficient CNN inference by eliminating off-chip weight transfers; however, peripheral control logic introduces three inefficiencies: bit- slice over-activation at reduced precision (L1), unnecessary accumula- tion depth (L2), and idle precision-transition stalls (L3). To address these, we present four synthesizable peripheral blocks: a Flush-Merge Enable (FME) controller, a Confidence-Based Early-Exit (EE) module, a Precision Register with Decoder (PR/PD), and a Bit-Serial Cycle Controller (CC), co-designed to minimize switching activity, wordline overhead, and leakage. Implemented in TSMC 65-nm CMOS at 335 MHz, the peripheral framework occupies 1769.760 μm2 post-synthesis and 1982.131 μm2 post-PnR. items.title: A Fast and Memory-Efficient Algorithm for Searching Faint Moving Objects using Synthetic Tracking
items.abstract: Detecting unknown faint moving objects using optical imaging is challenging. Long exposure times are infeasible for such targets, as the resulting image streaking causes a loss of signal-to-noise ratio due to energy dispersal across multiple pixels. To address this, synthetic tracking, a track-before-detect method, replaces long exposures with many short exposures, integrating them in post-processing to recover the moving signal. Enabled by modern CMOS detectors with fast readout and low read noise, this technique synthesizes telescope tracking by searching over a grid of velocities. However, the conventional brute-force implementation imposes a significant computational burden: integrating N_f frames of size (N_x,N_y) requires O(N_x N_y N_f^3) operations. items.title: Back-End-Of-Line Integration of 2-Terminal Ferroelectric Hafnia Synaptic Weights on Commercial CMOS Process
items.abstract: Functionalising the back-end-of-line (BEOL) of CMOS with emerging materials is a key route to neural network accelerators and neuromorphic systems. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time the integration of 2-terminal ferroelectric synaptic weights in the BEOL of as-delivered commercial 180 nm CMOS dies. A novel material stack is proposed, in which a WOx/[HfO2-ZrO2] bilayer is sandwiched between TiN and Mo electrodes. For devices annealed at 450 °C, programming below 1.8 V is achieved with a cycle-to-cycle variation below 3 %. Synaptic weights annealed at 500 °C exhibit more gradual weight updates, while the tested underlying NMOS transistors remain functional after the complete integration process. The trade-off between thermal budget and on-device training performance is illustrated using hardware-aware neural network simulations.

items.title: Demonstration of high output power (3.75 W/mm) with 31.8% PAE in Ga-Polar AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on sapphire at 94 GHz
items.abstract: In this work, a recessed-gate Ga-polar AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) on sapphire incorporating an AlGaN back-barrier for W-band operation is demonstrated. The device achieves a subthreshold slope of ~130 mV/dec, a peak transconductance of 0.75 S/mm, and an fmax exceeding 240 GHz. Continuous-wave load-pull measurements at 94 GHz show an output power of 3.75 W/mm with a power-added efficiency of 31.8%. This performance significantly exceeds the best previously reported Ga-polar devices on sapphire and approaches that of state-of-the-art Ga-polar devices on SiC, which provides a promising pathway toward high-performance W-band devices.

items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin-photon interfaces are essential for scalable quantum networks, but their realization requires optically bright transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent control. Donor-bound electron spins in II-VI semiconductors offer an attractive platform for optically active spin qubits because they combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions in a direct-bandgap material with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here we demonstrate optical initialization, coherent control, and readout of a single donor-bound electron spin in ZnSe. Using spin-selective donor-bound exciton optical transitions, we initialize the electron spin and directly resolve its spin-relaxation dynamics. We achieve coherent spin control with off-resonant picosecond optical pulses, as demonstrated...

items.title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
items.abstract: Buried interfaces play a critical role in the operational stability of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet remain challenging to probe non-destructively. Here, we demonstrate a multiwavelength photoluminescence-based approach exploiting the wavelength-dependent absorption of perovskites, enabling fast, and non-destructive probing of depth-sensitive degradation behavior of perovskite devices under operational conditions. Using ultraviolet (UV) light-soaking with different indium tin oxide (ITO) modifiers as a test case, we employ wide-field photoluminescence (PL) imaging, time-resolved photoluminescence (trPL) and ideality factor measurements with different wavelength excitation to characterize degradation behavior of both perovskite thin films and photovoltaic devices under UV soaking. items.title: Generation of quantum light with tunable Wigner negativity with a semiconductor quantum dot
items.abstract: Wigner-negative states of light are key resources for quantum advantage in continuous-variable optical quantum computing. They can be produced probabilistically via frequency conversion and photon detection, or deterministically by exploiting the single-photon nonlinearity of a quantum emitter. Here, we generate such Wigner-negative states of light with a tunable negativity using a single semiconductor quantum dot in a cavity. Optical coherent control of the quantum-dot transition allows to generate a quantum superposition of zero and one photon. The generated quantum states are characterized point-by-point in the phase space through homodyne measurement. The emergence of Wigner-function negativity is observed as the excitation power is increased. items.title: Bringing Hardware Security Education to All: A Seamless Curriculum Integration Approach
items.abstract: Cybersecurity education has predominantly focused on software and network security, under the assumption that the underlying hardware is trustworthy. Threats introduced through the global semiconductor supply chain, together with vulnerabilities arising during design and integration, challenge the assumption that hardware can serve as an unquestioned root of trust. Sensor-enabled systems and machine-learning accelerators further expand the hardware attack surface. The undergraduate curriculum of electrical and computer engineering and computer science programs has not evolved accordingly. Core courses cover the design and the functionality of hardware while the security aspects remain overlooked, and dedicated hardware security (HS) courses are elective, scarce, and often restricted to graduate students. Multimode continuous-variable quantum key distribution with CMOS-compatible photonic-electronic integration
items.abstract: Multiplexing and photonic-electronic integration offer a route to scalable and high-throughput quantum key distribution (QKD) networks through parallel transmission and compact hardware suited to volume manufacturing. Realizing this route requires multichannel transmitters and receivers, and a security analysis accounting for mode coupling. Here we present a CMOS-compatible photonic-electronic multimode continuous-variable QKD architecture, using polarization multiplexing as a two-mode example. Silicon-photonic transmitter and receiver chips prepare and detect two polarization modes in parallel. The receiver is co-integrated with a dual-channel 28-nm CMOS transimpedance amplifier, providing shot-noise clearances exceeding 20 dB in both channels. items.title: Optical Thermometry in Monolayer WS2: Raman and Photoluminescence Spectroscopy from 5 K to 1273 K
items.abstract: Reliable temperature measurement is essential for characterizing and engineering two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor devices, yet optical thermometry of 2D materials has so far been demonstrated only over narrow temperature windows spanning a few hundred kelvin. Here, we establish a comprehensive optical thermometry framework for monolayer WS2 from 5~K to 1273~K. We show that: (i) the out-of-plane A1g Raman mode shifts linearly with temperature above 100~K, with a slope of -0.0138 cm^{-1}/K in non-encapsulated WS2 (fitted over 298-1223~K) and a measurably smaller slope of -0.0121 cm^{-1}/K in an hBN-encapsulated sample (fitted over 100-1273~K); (ii) photoluminescence spectra measured over the same 5--1273~K range provide an independent optical indicator of the temperature: the neutral-exciton emission redshifts continuously with temperature and is well described by the semi-empirical Päss...

items.title: A van der Waals Floating-Gate Platform for Broadband Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Artificial synapses that integrate nonvolatile memory with broadband optoelectronic learning are essential for next-generation neuromorphic computing. However, their realization remains challenging because conventional floating-gate memories exhibit limited optical functionality and poor scalability. Here, we report a van der Waals ReS2/hBN/InSe floating-gate synaptic transistor that combines efficient charge storage with broadband optoelectronic learning in a single device architecture. The heterostructure incorporates InSe as a floating-gate layer for stable charge storage, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as a tunneling dielectric, and ReS2 as a photoresponsive channel, enabling carrier tunneling under electrical and optical stimulation. items.title: Photoinduced charging and spatially selective photochemistry on ferroelectric surfaces
items.abstract: Ferroelectric surfaces exhibit polarization-dependent photoreactivity and provide a route to program chemical patterns through local electrical control of polarization. Observations accumulated over several decades show reaction products in domain interiors, at domain boundaries, and in other selected regions, indicating that the mechanisms extend beyond a single polarization-induced band-bending picture. Here we analyze light-induced charging and interfacial reactions on uniformly polarized ferroelectrics and domain patterns, for dry surfaces and surfaces in contact with an electrochemically active solution. items.title: ChroNoC: A Tableless TDM Circuit-Switched NoC With Delay-Aware Deployment for Time-Sensitive Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Time-sensitive neuromorphic architectures require predictable interconnects to preserve precise event timing. Statically scheduled time-division-multiplexed (TDM) circuit-switched networks-on-chip (NoCs) provide deterministic latency at the cost of linear configuration-memory scaling with schedule depth. Furthermore, jointly optimizing task placement, routing, and scheduling creates an intractable combinatorial search space. Existing deployment frameworks also ignore algorithmic axonal delays by forcing immediate spike injections that increase network contention. This paper proposes a hardware-software co-design to address these challenges. ChroNoC is a tableless TDM NoC that embeds precomputed full-grid broadcast trees into combinational logic as a fixed routing substrate. items.title: Nonreciprocal magneto-optic beam steering of thermal emission
items.abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which ties absorptivity to emissivity and places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies and sensing systems. This constraint can be overcome using magneto-optic materials, which exhibit nonreciprocal thermal emission under an applied magnetic field. While the spectral nonreciprocity of magneto-optic devices has been explored theoretically and experimentally, nonreciprocal control over the direction of thermal emission has received far less attention. Here, we propose and numerically demonstrate nonreciprocal beam steering of thermal emission, wherein an applied magnetic field lifts the degeneracy between guided modes at +/- kx, enabling asymmetric and tunable directional thermal emission. items.title: Emergent parafermions with tunable localization in a quantum circuit network
items.abstract: \noindent Quantum circuit simulators with hybrid metal-semiconductor dots provide a versatile platform to realize Kondo anyons. These arise at critical points driven by frustrated Kondo screening of dot charge degrees of freedom and have been demonstrated experimentally in linear circuits of one or two dots. Here we study a triangular triple dot device, where geometric frustration gives rise to an emergent $\mathbb{Z}_3$ parafermion shared among the three dots. We show that the parafermion can be tunably relocated to any pair of dots by applying gate voltages, and is supported in both the weak-tunneling `Kondo limit' and the strong transmission `quasiballistic' regime. The critical states survive strong coupling to external leads and other dots, establishing the basis for a scalable and reconfigurable network architecture in which non-Abelian excitations can be realized and manipulated.

Motivated by this observation, we develop a decision-theoretic framework in which Protective Response Intensity (PRI) is an endogenous decision variable. We introduce Response-Induced Loss (RIL) to capture costs generated by defensive actions and characterize a unique optimal response that balances disruption mitigation against self-induced losses. items.title: A Rowhammer attack on Fil-C's software capabilities
items.abstract: Rowhammer is a hardware vulnerability in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) in which repeated accesses to one or more aggressor rows can induce bit-flips in nearby victim rows. This phenomenon violates a core assumption of conventional programming language semantics: that reading from or writing to one memory location does not modify others. Despite the security importance of this phenomenon, there is no widely established formal framework connecting Rowhammer faults with program behaviour. This makes it difficult to reason rigorously about the efficacy of proposed Rowhammer defences and the program-level guarantees they provide. To address this gap, we present a probabilistic small-step operational semantics for an idealised imperative language subject to Rowhammer-style faults. items.title: Optical imaging with only the evanescent fields and without diffraction
items.abstract: We report on a conceptual framework for optical imaging utilizing exclusively evanescent fields, effectively eliminating or attenuating standard optical diffraction. We present the theoretical foundation of this concept based on the decomposition of dipole radiation into evanescent fields and homogeneous propagating waves, exploring the explicit conditions required to suppress the latter. By successfully decoupling and removing the homogeneous component, optical tasks, such as sub-diffraction imaging, can be executed solely via evanescent channels, bypassing traditional diffractive limits. We discuss the physical feasibility of this approach and provide concrete examples of how this conjecture can be realized using currently available laboratory and industrial techniques. items.title: Charge state and hydration of vacancies in silicon and silicon carbide in contact with water: A grand-canonical first-principles stability map
items.abstract: The state of a vacancy in a semiconductor is normally described by the Fermi level alone. In wet-etched, electrochemically processed, or humid silicon and silicon carbide, a vacancy also takes up hydrogen and oxygen from water, in amounts set by pH and electrode potential. We treat both effects together by minimizing the grand potential of a vacancy complex over its charge state and hydrogen/oxygen content. The result is a stability map in Fermi level and hydrogen chemical potential, which the computational hydrogen electrode relates to pH and potential. We parameterize it with spin-polarized density functional theory in 64-atom cells, including the vibrational free energy of bound H and O, for the silicon vacancy, its H, O, and OH complexes, and both vacancies of 3C-SiC. items.title: Physics Informed Neural Networks for Solving the Drift-Diffusion Equations
items.abstract: The drift-diffusion equations are the fundamental building block for the modeling, design, and optimization of modern semiconductor devices. Solutions of the drift-diffusion equations rarely give way to analytical forms, and exhibit strong nonlinearity, with the solutions ranging over several orders of magnitude. These attributes have led to research into numerical solvers, and while many commercial Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) packages now exist, they may require long simulation times, exhibit sensitivity to initial guesses, and rely on mesh generation. Further, these solvers are not well suited for inverse problems where the design parameters of a device are retrieved from its desired functional characteristics. items.title: Intrinsic Raman Modes and Crystal Symmetry of Altermagnetic $α$-MnTe
items.abstract: Crystal symmetry governs the physical properties of materials and provides the framework for interpreting their microscopic excitations and macroscopic responses. In altermagnets, the crystal symmetries that relate opposite-spin sublattices give rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting despite compensated magnetization. Determining the real crystal symmetry is therefore essential for understanding the intrinsic electronic and magnetic properties. For the altermagnetic semiconductor $α$-MnTe, conflicting Raman assignments have left both its intrinsic lattice excitations and its crystal symmetry unresolved. This enables us to evaluate the accuracy and speedup under a very wide range of SPICE simulations, benchmarking our models against an industry-standard implementation. Since standard cell library characterization involves thousands of SPICE simulations, it serves as a gr...

Kimi K3 instead entered at broadly frontier prices and generated a market reaction concentrated more heavily among rival Chinese AI laboratories. items.title: Localization Contrast As a Fundamental Limit of Radiative Quantum Efficiency
items.abstract: Disorder can localize valence- and conduction-band states to different degrees, yet whether such localization contrast has observable consequences remains poorly understood. Here, we show that localization contrast strongly impacts competing carrier-recombination channels. We illustrate this behavior in random In$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N alloys. Increasing the In content from $x=13.5\%$ to $x=22\%$ progressively localizes the valence-band maximum state while leaving the conduction-band minimum state comparatively delocalized. This contrasting localization decreases the interband optical momentum matrix element underlying radiative recombination. For Auger-Meitner recombination, however, localization alone does not determine the coupling; atomic-scale disorder also breaks primitive-cell translational symmetry and modifies the momentum-space and phase structure of the states. This generates addition...

items.abstract: In this work we theoretically study the structural transformations occurring in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) subjected to strong deformations. The first-principle computer simulations are based on the density functional theory employing the pseudopotentials with the exchange-correlation energy given in Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof form. It is found that, under certain shear strains, there can form an ordered 2D orthorhombic phase with the 2D layer space symmetry pmmm. Thermal stability of the latter up to ~900 K is demonstrated by first-principle Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics. items.title: Electrically Pumped Quadratic-Soliton Mode-Locked Laser in Lithium Niobate Nanophotonics
items.abstract: Femtosecond mode-locked lasers are the workhorse of modern photonics, enabling optical atomic clocks, frequency combs, precision spectroscopy, and ultrafast signal processing. Bringing them onto nanophotonic chips promises miniaturized ultrafast systems, yet combining femtosecond pulse generation with electrical pumping remains a major challenge, rooted in a trade-off between the speed and energy efficiency of mode-locking mechanisms. Kerr-based mechanisms offer nearly instantaneous response but typically require high intracavity peak powers that are difficult to achieve with nanophotonic-compatible semiconductor gain. Conversely, semiconductor saturable absorbers enable strong nonlinear responses at low energies but are limited by their slow carrier dynamics. Here we break this trade-off by introducing quadratic-soliton mode-locking based on a quadratic nonlinear interferometer (QNLI):...

items.abstract: Recently, two-dimensional goldene, a single-atomic-layer gold sheet, has been experimentally realized and is expected to be a promising material for next-generation devices, offering new possibilities beyond three-dimensional bulk gold. Because quasi-one-dimensional derivatives can exhibit properties markedly different from their two-dimensional counterparts, we investigate the stability, electronic, and magnetic properties of goldene-based nanoribbons (GOLDNRs) using first-principles computational methods. Our findings demonstrate that the electronic structure of these nanoribbons depends strongly on both edge chirality and ribbon width. Depending on the boundary configuration, the systems can exhibit semiconducting behavior with electronic band gaps of approximately 0.77 eV and 0.04 eV, or retain metallic characteristics. Additionally, the edge regions act as electronically active site...

items.title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference exhibits distinct computational characteristics across its two phases: prefill is compute-intensive, whereas decode is more memory-bound. As a result, AI accelerators achieve varying levels of efficiency across the two phases. GPUs are well suited to prefill, but are often underutilized during decode. By contrast, NPUs can utilize their compute resources more effectively during decode. Motivated by this observation, we explore a heterogeneous architecture that integrates GPUs and NPUs, mapping prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs to achieve high performance and efficiency. However, realizing such heterogeneous integration is challenging because LLM phase disaggregation requires KV cache transfer from prefill to decode (that is, from GPUs to NPUs), which is complicated by differences in inter-device communication mechanisms and KV cache tensor layouts. Here, we develop an NEGF-based approach to systematically and rapidly evaluate the defect sensitivity of electron transport in materials without depending on material-specific defect geometries. items.title: Observation of Size-dependent Optical Modes and Confinement in Fin Cavities using Angle-Resolved Cathodoluminescence
items.abstract: We observe novel optical fringes and emission coherence in laterally formed semiconductor fins using wavelength- and angle-resolved cathodoluminescence (WARCL). These findings demonstrate that cavity mode and emission confinement are directly governed by cavity geometry including cavity dimensions, facet angles, and orientation. In flat fins narrowing the width from 3000 nm to 200 nm sharpens fringe intensity, indicating stronger mode confinement and increased coherence. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations confirm that the observed fringes originate from internal reflections among the fin facets, consistent with a Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity model where the cavity length determines the fringe spacing. FDTD also reveals a transition from multi-mode to single-longitudinal-mode behavior in 200-nm fins, consistent with experimentally observed fringe narrowing. Increasing fin length...

items.abstract: Large anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) usually relies on magnetic ordering, which fixes a preferred moment orientation and couples it to charge transport. The magnetization is described by an effective S = 1/2 model with an anisotropic g-factor ratio of g_c/g_ab = 1.43(1). items.title: Coherent dynamics and ultrafast evolution of optical nonlinearity of self-hybridized exciton-polaritons in WSe2
items.abstract: Exciton-polaritons (EPs) are valuable for investigating macroscopic quantum coherent phenomena. However, overcoming the rapid decoherence of EPs under ambient conditions is challenging, even using delicately fabricated optical cavities. Here, we show pronounced coherent dynamics in thin flakes of WSe2 supporting self-hybridized EPs. Ultrafast two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy (2DES) resolves two types of quantum beating: Rabi oscillation with a period of ~ 24 fs and a slower, ~ 50 fs period oscillation, revealing coherent coupling not only between excitons and cavity, but also between polaritons and dark states. Rapid evolution of 2DES line shape indicates a change of dominant optical nonlinearities from Rabi contraction of polaritons to many-body interactions of excitons in the first 100 fs, marking the transition from coherent to incoherent polariton excitations. items.title: The Spectroscopic Atlas of Excitonic Complexes in hBN-Encapsulated S-TMD Monolayers: From Excitons to Oxcitons and Beyond
items.abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) encapsulation has transformed the optical spectroscopy of semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers (MLs) by suppressing extrinsic disorder and enabling the resolution of an increasingly complex hierarchy of excitonic states. This Review provides a spectroscopy-oriented framework for understanding and identifying excitonic complexes in hBN-encapsulated Mo- and W-based MLs and their alloys. The discussion covers bright and dark excitons, Rydberg states, charged excitons, biexcitons, phonon-assisted replicas, and higher-order Fermi-sea many-body states, including hexcitons and oxcitons, with an emphasis on the experimental signatures that distinguish them. Particular attention is given to the combined use of photoluminescence and absorption-related spectroscopy, electrostatic gating, polarization analysis, excitation-power and temperature depen...

items.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing
items.abstract: Conventional wafer defect analysis relies on offline, closed-world classifiers that fail to detect novel, unseen defect signatures emerging during continuous semiconductor manufacturing. To address this, we propose WaferHDC, an online open-world wafer defect discovery framework based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC). The memory-centric architecture of WaferHDC enables rapid anomaly detection and grouping of recurring failures into compact hypervector representations. This allows the memory space to dynamically scale with new defect modes without retraining a static classifier or archiving entire raw wafer history. WaferHDC first models normal spatial distributions, then dynamically groups recurring failures into persistent defect memory without labels or predefined class counts. It outperforms the strongest online baseline by 13.3 p.p. in adjusted Rand index and 10.5 p.p. in normalize...

items.title: Ultrafast and Anisotropic Exciton Transport in Layered NbOI$_2$
items.abstract: Ferroelectric layered semiconductors provide a unique platform for exploring coupled excitonic and electronic phenomena in reduced dimensions. Here, exciton transport in layered NbOI$_2$ is investigated using transient absorption microscopy. Ultrafast and strongly anisotropic exciton diffusion is observed. The diffusion coefficient of about 160 cm$^2$ s$^{-1}$ along the nonpolar crystal axis is among the highest reported for van der Waals semiconductors. The transport exhibits an approximately twofold in-plane anisotropy between the polar and nonpolar directions, reflecting the intrinsic low-symmetry crystal structure of NbOI$_2$. The environmental stability of NbOI$_2$ is further investigated, and fabrication and encapsulation conditions required to achieve long-term sample stability are identified. items.title: Accelerating real-time hybrid-functional calculations with learned ACE and symmetry-based FFT reuse
items.abstract: Real-time hybrid-functional calculations require repeated reconstruction of nonlocal exchange, whose cost grows rapidly with Brillouin-zone sampling. We develop two methods to improve the efficiency of time evolution and spatial processing. The first learns the time evolution of adaptively compressed exchange (ACE) factors and predicts their updates, reducing the frequency of explicit reconstruction. The second uses crystal symmetry to reuse exchange fast Fourier transforms (FFTs) among equivalent real-space points. This symmetry-based FFT reuse (SBFR) reduces the number of FFTs while retaining the full $\bm k$-point sum. The methods can be used with a variety of hybrid functionals, and we use HSE06 in this work. items.title: Nanophotonic Extreme Ultraviolet Polarimeter
items.abstract: Nanophotonic engineering has revolutionized how we manipulate the polarization of visible light. Here, we extend such control to extreme ultraviolet radiation, the spectral region of attosecond science and semiconductor lithography, where transmissive optical elements are lacking. We implement channel waveguides that restrict incident 41-nm-wavelength light to a few modes with defined spatial profiles and propagation constants. By designing the propagation-length-dependent interference of two eigenmodes, we achieve polarization-dependent forward scattering, which we exploit to create a transmissive nanophotonic analyzer that resolves the polarization axis and spectrum of extreme ultraviolet light from a single measurement. items.abstract: We develop a product phylogenetic network framework for examining anchored exploration. Using 102,465 semiconductor products grouped into 45,996 design families, we distinguish accumulated design continuity (Anchor) from externally precedented feature additions (horizontal transfer, HT). These patterns connect technological trajectories and recombination by distinguishing the continuity associated with incorporating external features from that associated with reproducing them in subsequent products.

At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.1-7.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies, over three decades of concentration. This paper presents SimSkip, a successive-approximation-register (SAR) skipping scheme that combines a lightweight StrongARM-comparator similarity detector with SAR-skipping-aware training. When two held voltages are similar, the upper bits of the preceding code are reused to skip SAR comparisons. Detector-induced disturbance extracted from 55-nm CMOS simulations and bit-exact prefix saturation are embedded in the forward pass, and the network learns to tolerate them through quantization-aware training and knowledge distillation. items.title: A semiconductor photon-pair source based on a polariton cascade
items.abstract: We present a theoretical study of a semiconductor photon-pair source based on a radiative cascade enabled by a permanent exciton dipole. The source consists of a GaAs quantum dot placed between a metal nanoparticle and a mirror. The dot exciton and the localized electromagnetic mode mix to form upper and lower polaritons. Without a permanent dipole, a symmetry separating states with even and odd excitation numbers forbids photon emission between the polaritons. Separation of the mean electron and hole positions gives the exciton a permanent dipole and breaks this symmetry. The upper polariton can then emit an idler photon as it decays to the lower polariton. The lower polariton can emit a signal photon as the system returns to its ground state. Using an effective model, we calculate the probability that a prepared upper polariton emits both photons through the metal antenna. We also anal...

The approach includes conventional ground-state FNOs together with state-specific (SS-FNO) and state-averaged (SA-FNO) variants constructed from perturbative one-particle density matrices. We implement these approximations for periodic Moller-Plesset perturbation theory, algebraic diagrammatic construction, and equation-of-motion coupled cluster methods in the PySCF software package and benchmark them for correlation energies, equations of state, fundamental band gaps, and quasiparticle band structures of semiconductors and insulators. items.title: JANUS: A Multi-modal Foundation Neural Sampler for Disordered Materials
items.abstract: Disordered materials are central to modern technologies, from high-performance alloys to quantum devices, yet understanding and designing them requires exploring an enormous space of compositions and atomic arrangements. Here we introduce JANUS, a multimodal neural sampler that jointly explores chemical composition, atomic structure and volume, learning directly from the energy of the system without requiring pre-generated equilibrium configurations. Across test systems, JANUS reproduces reference equilibrium properties and recovers free energy and phase behavior with about three orders of magnitude fewer energy evaluations than reference Monte Carlo sampling. In multicomponent alloys, JANUS reproduces experimentally observed local chemical order and can be steered to further enhance chemical order and stiffness. items.title: Inverse-Designed High-Q and Small-Mode-Volume Silicon Nitride Photonic Crystal Cavities for Second- and Third-Harmonic Generation
items.abstract: SiN photonic crystal (PhC) cavities are promising platforms for nonlinear and quantum photonics because of their wide transparency window, CMOS compatibility, and negligible two-photon absorption. However, realizing high-Q/V cavities remains challenging because of the relatively low refractive index of SiN. Here, we employ inverse design to optimize a two-dimensional SiN PhC cavity and experimentally demonstrate a quality factor of approximately 80,000, the highest reported for a near-stoichiometric SiN 2D PhC cavity. Furthermore, both second- and third-harmonic generation are observed from the same cavity, providing experimental evidence of strong optical confinement and large Q/V. Our results establish inverse-designed SiN PhC cavities as a promising platform for nonlinear photonics and future heterogeneous integrated photonic devices.

To address this, we demonstrate a gradient-descent feedback approach in a silicon double quantum dot device using high-bandwidth radio-frequency (rf) reflectometry readout and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) for digital signal processing. This architecture enables continuous multi-parameter gradient calculation and quick gate voltage updates, significantly increasing the effective feedback bandwidth compared to previous methods relying on slow direct-current transport measurements. By operating with 8 steps per feedback cycle and an integration time of 25.6 $μ$s, this high-speed stabilization scheme maintains better than -6 dB of noise suppression up to 5 kHz, achieving an attenuation of $-7.4 \pm 0.2$ dB at the maximum measured frequency. We show that commutative factorizations of Liénard equations are gauge-conjugated forms of the nonlocal linearizing transformation of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Kundu and Lakshmanan, the factorization constant being half the difference of the roots of the associated linear oscillator. The application of strain modifies the exciton energy landscape and, in particular, the relative energy separation between bright and dark exciton states. The impact of strain on the transient photoluminescence and diffusion of non-equilibrium excitons has remained largely unexplored so far. items.title: THz-Driven Floquet Spin Valve-Modulator
items.abstract: Within the scattering matrix ($S$-matrix) framework adapted to the high-frequency Floquet--Magnus formalism based on the length gauge, we investigate spin-dependent quantum transport in a 1D quantum ring with an asymmetric ($π/2$) configuration of quantum point contacts. We demonstrate the realization of a contactless electromagnetic analog of the Datta--Das spin field-effect transistor with ferromagnetic leads operating at zero static magnetic field. It is shown that an off-resonance terahertz (THz) field enables high-precision switching between spin channels without altering the static parameters of the nanostructure. Driven by an electronic Vernier effect, the quantum interference in the asymmetric geometry yields a selective spin phase rotator alongside an ultra-high-contrast current-suppression regime (``optical shutter''). items.title: Decoherence of a quantum magneto-oscillator: Effect of field-bath interaction
items.abstract: We investigate the quantum dissipative dynamics of a charged magneto-oscillator(CMO) coupled to a heat bath of harmonic oscillators in the presence of an additional field-bath interaction. The problem is formulated within the framework of the generalized quantum Langevin equation, where the external confining potential modifies the random force correlations and the memory kernel of the environment, and the effective spring constant. Using the corresponding non-Markovian master equation, we examine the influence of the field-bath coupling on the temporal decay of the reduced density matrix of the system. We show that the additional interaction leads to an enhancement of the decoherence rate by altering the dissipative response of the bath. Thus our results shed light on the role of field-bath coupling in the quantum to classical transition of a CMO. The resulting fluctuation-dissipation r...

items.title: Parity-selected charging and noise-correlated work retention in a coupled Si/SiGe double quantum dot battery: theory and experimentally parameterized modeling
items.abstract: We investigate extractable work storage in a capacitively coupled double quantum dot (DQD) quantum battery (QB) subjected to experimentally motivated detuning charge noise. The battery is modeled as two interacting charge qubits with an Ising-type capacitive coupling and is charged by resonant microwave modulation of the tunnel coupling channel. Detuning fluctuations are introduced as classical stochastic processes generated from a band-limited 1/f noise spectrum. For each noise realization, the evolution remains unitary, whereas decoherence and loss of contrast emerge after ensemble averaging. We analyze the total ergotropy, its population and coherent contributions, the energy basis populations, a passive ordering violation diagnostic, and the Jensen-Shannon coherence of the noise-averaged state. The results show that resonant tunnel coupling driving selects a dominant E0 E3 population...

items.title: High-Fidelity Synthetic Transmission Electron Microscopy Image Generation Using Diffusion Probabilistic Models for Data-Limited Semiconductor Metrology
items.abstract: Advanced semiconductor nodes drastically increased demand for Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), yet destructive sample preparation, slow imaging and high costs severely limit the availability of diverse datasets needed for downstream machine learning (ML). Synthetic data generation is becoming essential, but current generative models often miss TEM-specific noise, structural detail, and stochastic variability crucial for evaluation. We present a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) framework for synthetic TEM image generation under extreme data scarcity. A progressive patch-based training strategy scales from low-resolution patches to full images, enabling from-scratch training with only 15 samples. We integrate a custom TrivialAugment adaptation, cross-process domain transfer, classifier guidance, and RePaint-style inpainting, culminating in full-image generation that pr...

items.title: Dispersive mode coupling in $p$-doped semiconductor nanomechanical resonators
items.abstract: Dispersive coupling between vibrational modes with different frequencies is a major nonlinear dynamical effect. We show that in $p$-doped semiconductors such coupling is strongly enhanced. Moreover, the coupling parameters increase with the order of the nonlinearity. The doping-induced dispersive coupling becomes much stronger than the intrinsic one already for moderately strong doping. Its dependence on the hole density is nonmonotonic, and the temperature dependence becomes nonmonotonic for higher densities. Relevant mesoscopic frequency fluctuations are briefly discussed. The results are applied to Si resonators, where doping is used to compensate the temperature dependence of a clock mode, whereas another low-frequency mode is used as a thermometer to enable temperature stabilization.

items.title: Quantum digital simulations of time-domain semiconductor spectroscopy in the semi-classical approximation
items.abstract: We present a digital quantum simulation framework for ultrafast optical spectroscopy of semiconductor materials. The framework is based on Brillouin-zone discretization and is designed as a quantum alternative to classical simulations based on the semiconductor Bloch equations. Its current capabilities include quantum simulations of linear absorption and optical gain, incorporating Lorentzian broadening, finite-temperature band-filling effects, and reduced-dimensionality effects. Comparison with classical simulations of GaAs within the single-particle approximation demonstrates quantitative agreement in the noiseless limit. The inclusion of realistic hardware noise characteristic of NISQ-era quantum computers effectively manifests as an additional source of scattering, resulting in increased spectral broadening. items.title: Electrically tunable Crossed Andreev Reflection in Bipolar Magnetic Semiconductors
items.abstract: Crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) is a nonlocal quantum transport phenomenon that arises at the interfaces between a superconductor and two spatially separated metals. In this process, an electron incident from one metal combines with another electron originating from the other metal to form a Cooper pair in the SC. In this work, we theoretically investigate the quantum transport properties of a device comprising a central $s$-wave superconductor sandwiched between two bipolar magnetic semiconductor (BMS) leads. BMS materials possess a unique bandstructure where the conduction and valence bands are fully spin-polarized in opposite directions. By applying independent gate voltages to the two BMS leads, we selectively tune their chemical potentials to configure an antiparallel spin alignment at the Fermi energy.
